title: Kakunodate — 角館
goal: Recognise reading/writing words and distinguish characters from sentences.

cards.title: A Place for a Short Travel Note

blocks.text: Kakunodate is known for its preserved samurai-residence district. It is a historic district within present-day Semboku, and remains the fixed location lesson in the course plan. We will read a simple book and write one short travel note; we will not introduce difficult historical titles.
**角館で本を読みます。** かくのだてで ほんを よみます。 — I read a book in Kakunodate.
読む was assisted in Hiraizumi. Today the spelling becomes formal study, together with the writing words that make a simple notebook activity possible.

items: **Character:** 角 · **Orientation meaning/reading:** horn; corner/angle; つの/かど, カク · **Radical/components:** 角, つのへん/かく; whole horn-derived form · **Role:** Encounter. Its interior resembles other shapes but is not simply 月.
**Character:** 館 · **Orientation meaning/reading:** building/hall; カン; だて here · **Radical/components:** 食 in 飠/しょくへん form, plus 官, a historical sound component · **Role:** Review encounter from 函館.

blocks.text: **角館 / かくのだて** is learned as a whole. The name's の and だて cannot be inferred by reading every character in isolation. **函館 / はこだて** and 角館 share 館. The food radical inside a hall character is a knowledge connection, not a requirement that the building must be a restaurant.

cards.title: 読む Becomes a Formal Word

blocks.text: **読む / よむ — read; 読みます / よみます — read/will read.** 読 has radical **言**, ごんべん, and a right **売**-shaped section in the modern form. The right side belongs to a historical sound structure; recognise its modern shape rather than defining reading as “selling words.”
**本を読みます。** ほんを よみます。 — I read a book.
**この本は読みません。** この ほんは よみません。 — I do not read this book, with the book made the topic.
読む/読みました/読みませんでした retain 読 while the kana ending changes. Review the polite verb pattern; we are not teaching a new reading for every inflected form.

**書く / かく — write; 書きます / かきます — write/will write.** 書 is indexed under **曰**, ひらび/いわく. The upper **聿**-like brush/hand shape is a recognition and writing-related connection. The lower section resembles 日 but indexing 曰 and ordinary 日 are not automatically the same component.
**ノートに書きます。** ノートに かきます。 — I write in a notebook.

ノート is a notebook, written in katakana. に marks the surface/place where writing is put, while **角館で書きます** uses で for the location of the writing action. Different nouns lead to different relationships; the lesson gives clear examples rather than a universal rule for every writing context.

**文 / ぶん — sentence; 短い文 / みじかいぶん — a short sentence.** 短い is assisted vocabulary for this phrase; 短 is not formal study here. 文 is its own radical, ぶん. Recognise the whole crossing shape, not a forced sum of ordinary modern component meanings.
**文を読みます。** ぶんを よみます。 — I read a sentence.
**文を書きます。** ぶんを かきます。 — I write a sentence.

A sentence communicates a complete thought in this activity. Today's examples contain full predicate endings such as です or ました; we do not demand a technical grammar analysis of every kind of Japanese sentence.
**字 / じ — character/letter; 漢字 / かんじ — kanji; 文字 / もじ — character(s), writing.** 漢 is an assisted character inside the familiar whole word 漢字.
字 has radical **子**, こ, under **宀**, うかんむり. These are visible recognition pieces. A remembered child-under-roof image is not enough to explain all uses of 字.
**この字は大きいです。** この じは おおきいです。 — This character is large.
**漢字を書きます。** かんじを かきます。 — I write kanji.
Distinguish 文 / ぶん, a sentence, from 字 / じ, a character. A sentence can contain several characters, kana and punctuation. 文字 is もじ as a whole word, not simply the standalone 文 reading plus じ.
**読書 / どくしょ — reading books.** This is a useful recognition compound of 読 and 書. It gives an on-reading connection; the action **本を読む** still uses よむ.
Compare:

items: 読む / よむ — to read.
書く / かく — to write.
読書 / どくしょ — reading books, a noun.

blocks.text: We do not require する grammar to use the noun here. **これは読書の本です** would describe a book about reading and is not our necessary model. Prefer the already natural **本を読みます** for an action. Recognise a useful compound without forcing it into a sentence that introduces another unexplained construction.
**角館でノートに文を書きました。** かくのだてで ノートに ぶんを かきました。 — I wrote a sentence in a notebook in Kakunodate.
Group it: 角館で / ノートに / 文を / 書きました. The place of the activity is marked で; the notebook where the writing is put uses に; the sentence written uses を; the verb gives past time.
**紙 / かみ — paper**, with assisted 紙. **紙に字を書きます。** かみに じを かきます。 — I write a character on paper. We teach the whole word, while the difficult character remains helped.

cards.title: A Note We Can Already Understand

blocks.text: Write this fictional diary sentence:
**秋田でご飯を食べました。** あきたで ごはんを たべました。 — I ate a meal in Akita.
Then read it: **この文を読みます。** この ぶんを よみます。 — I read this sentence.

Identify **秋田**, the place; **で**, action location; **ご飯を**, object; **食べました**, completed action. Writing and reading reinforce the same prior knowledge. We do not insert a difficult word merely to include each new character in one sentence. A useful note can be short and accurate.

items: **Action:** read · **Nonpast:** 読みます · **Negative:** 読みません · **Past:** 読みました · **Past negative:** 読みませんでした
**Action:** write · **Nonpast:** 書きます · **Negative:** 書きません · **Past:** 書きました · **Past negative:** 書きませんでした

blocks.text: Readings: よみます/よみません/よみました/よみませんでした; かきます/かきません/かきました/かきませんでした.
**本は読みました。でも、文は書きませんでした。** ほんは よみました。でも、ぶんは かきませんでした。 — I read the book. But I did not write a sentence.
は makes the contrasted objects topics. Do not teach that は can only appear once or only name a person. The ending, not the object topic, determines whether the action occurred.

items: Read 角館 and recall the other 館 place name from Hokkaido. **Answer:** かくのだて; 函館 / はこだて.
Read 読む, 書く, 文, 字. **Answer:** よむ, かく, ぶん, じ.
Which is the compound どくしょ? **Answer:** 読書.
Complete “write a sentence”: 文＿書きます。 **Answer:** を.
Complete “write in a notebook”: ノート＿書きます。 **Answer:** に.
Make 書きます past negative. **Answer:** 書きませんでした / かきませんでした.

blocks.text: 角館 is かくのだて; 館 reconnects with Hakodate. 読む/書く are よむ/かく. 文 is a sentence; 字 is a character; 漢字 and 文字 are whole words. 読書 is どくしょ. 書 is indexed under 曰, despite its lower section resembling 日. A writing activity can contain object を, surface に, and action place で.
**Recall task:** “I wrote a sentence in a notebook.” **Model:** ノートに文を書きました。 Continue to Yokote and give the note a daily time structure.
